overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law when a member of the public was removed from the April 12 Zoom meeting and could not rejoin, and the May 6 ratification did not cure it; the AG declined to review the claim that the complainant could not speak by phone and ordered future compliance without additional remedies.

allegations.summary: Complainant was removed from the Zoom video conference for the April 12 meeting and could not access it by video for a period, after a request to disable her video feed.
allegations.key_passage: the April 12 meeting was not accessible to all members of the public for the duration of the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant said she could not unmute or speak during the portion of the April 12 meeting she attended by telephone.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, even if true, an allegation that the Complainant was unable to actively participate in the April 12 meeting does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law and we therefore decline to review it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
